title: Build the Parking Lot LLD (Machine-Coding Round)
summary:
The most-asked machine-coding problem, built the way a strong candidate would build it in 90 minutes. You write clear entities (`Spot`, `Vehicle`, `Ticket`, `Receipt`), a pluggable **allocation strategy** (EV spots first, then smallest fit, then nearest to the entry gate), **pluggable fee rules in integer paise** (slab pricing with a grace period, wrapped by a daily-cap decorator), ticketed entry and exit, and an async **mutex** that keeps allocation correct under concurrent entries.

The judge fires 40 concurrent entries at 10 spots with seeded I/O jitter and checks that no spot or plate is ever double-booked. It then registers a **new vehicle type (bus)** with its own spot size and pricing, and the allocator must handle it without any code change. That is the open/closed principle, tested.

milestones.name: M1: Fee rules
milestones.description: `SlabFeeRule` (grace, slabs, per started hour beyond), `PerHourFeeRule`, and a `DailyCapFeeRule` decorator, all in integer paise with input validation.

milestones.name: M2: Allocation
milestones.description: `NearestSmallestFitStrategy`: EV preference, smallest fit, nearest to the gate, id tie-break. Regular cars never take EV spots. `LotFullError`, and validation of gate, type and pricing.

milestones.name: M3: Tickets and exit
milestones.description: Tickets record entry; exit computes the fee, frees the spot and closes the ticket. Double exit and duplicate plates are rejected.

milestones.name: M4: Concurrency
milestones.description: A FIFO `Mutex`; 40 concurrent entries for 10 spots give exactly 10 distinct spots; the same plate at two gates gets one ticket; concurrent double exit pays once.

milestones.name: M5: Extensibility
milestones.description: Register a `bus` type with a size-4 bay and its own pricing, with no allocator change. Inject a different allocation strategy (valet: farthest first).
